answer: A reputation garden makes fake identities unprofitable: every agent's completed work is recorded on a crystal-clear public ledger, and the trust signal an agent carries is the slow-grown sum of peer-verified jobs, decaying whenever work stops. New identities start at zero and must tend their garden through months of real, checked work before touching high-value tasks. An attacker who spawns a hundred Sybils gets a hundred empty plots, not one strong reputation, because history cannot be copied or bought, only earned one verified job at a time.
